messages.author: c621ac38989fbf3c
messages.subject: Intercept specification in formula
parts:
This is hopefully an easy question, but I'm trying to understand how the intercept syntax in INLA formulae differs from standard models in R.

In the how to file, this format is suggested:

formula <- y ~ 0 + b0 + x

So there is a b0 term for the intercept that seems to originate in the stack, with effects = list(b0 = 1)

But what about the 0? I'm accustomed to that being in regression models to fixing the intercept at the origin.

So I assume b0=1 means I do NOT want to fix the intercept --

But what is the difference between:
  y ~ 0 + b0 + x
  y ~ b0 + x
  y ~ 1 + b0 + x
  y ~ x (i.e. no intercept specified)

Thanks,
Paul

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Intercept specification in formula
parts: By example:

On 10/02/2017 13:36, Paul Lantos wrote:
> y ~ 0 + b0 + x
> y ~ b0 + x
> y ~ 1 + b0 + x
> y ~ x

> d <- data.frame(b0=1, x=1:3, y=-2:0)
> model.matrix(y ~ 0 + b0 + x, d)
b0 x
1 1 1
2 1 2
3 1 3
attr(,"assign")
[1] 1 2
> model.matrix(y ~ b0 + x, d)
(Intercept) b0 x
1 1 1 1
2 1 1 2
3 1 1 3
attr(,"assign")
[1] 0 1 2
> model.matrix(y ~ 1 + b0 + x, d)
(Intercept) b0 x
1 1 1 1
2 1 1 2
3 1 1 3
attr(,"assign")
[1] 0 1 2
> model.matrix(y ~ x, d)
(Intercept) x
1 1 1
2 1 2
3 1 3
attr(,"assign")
[1] 0 1

Elias

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Intercept specification in formula
parts: This is not to fix the intercept! This is just to add the column of ones explicit. When a model contain effects with different sizes, any may differ from the outcome size, them you need to make the intercept explicit as we have to do with the SPDE models. However, you should not have the default intercept from the formula plus the explicit one. So, it is why we take out the default intercept by having either +0 or -1 in the formula.
